body:
Good morning, Kern County — it’s Wednesday, September 9. The conversation around school safety continues today after last night’s Kern High School District board meeting, where parents and advocates again pushed for stronger security at football games and campus events. Expect a hot one: temperatures climbing to near 100, air quality moderate at 62, and no active alerts or fires on the horizon.

## The Kern Overnight

Fire crews and deputies had a busy night across Bakersfield and the county. Just after midnight, a passerby spotted smoke coming from a building near Mount Vernon Avenue and Niles Street in east Bakersfield, in the area of a nearby discount store, and the call drew multiple engines, two trucks, and battalion chiefs to the scene. Crews knocked the fire down within about 15 minutes, completed a primary search, and stayed on site for roughly half an hour; no injuries were reported. Around 5 a.m., a vehicle in a hotel parking lot on Marriott Drive struck a parked car and caught fire, and a caller worried that someone might still be inside the burning vehicle, so firefighters and an ambulance were dispatched. In the Hageman Road area, a grass fire smoldered with light smoke overnight, but crews said it was contained to an irrigation area with no immediate threat; they made contact with the landowner and planned to return in the morning with equipment to finish putting it out.

Deputies also responded to two possible domestic incidents. One was in the Paramount Colony area, where a caller said a driver holding a toddler had left an In-N-Out parking lot in a dark sedan; the vehicle’s direction remained unknown. Another was on White Lane before dawn, where a neighbor heard a woman screaming and a man shouting, and dispatchers kept an open line with a crying woman while officers made their way to the apartment complex. Other calls included medical aid staged near 2nd Street after an apparent assault, a welfare check on a man and woman reported sleeping in the canal area along Gosford Road, an officer response to a Brown Street home for a man with blood on his clothing who was off his medications, and a request from a stranded motorist on Interstate 5 north of Quebec who said she had been broken down on the shoulder since the previous day and wanted help getting off the freeway.

## Today's weather

The current reading at Meadows Field is 77 degrees, and the valley is heading toward a high near 100 with an overnight low around 75. No heat advisories or other weather alerts are active for Kern County. Air quality checks in at a moderate 62 on the AQI scale, so anyone sensitive to particulate matter might want to limit time outdoors in the afternoon. No active fires are burning in the county this morning, and conditions look calm, dry, and hot.

## Top stories

**The Kern High School District heard another round of community calls for stronger safety measures on Tuesday night,** 23ABC reports. The meeting came more than two weeks after a gunman killed 17-year-old Levi Brown at an Independence High football game, a tragedy that prompted student walkouts demanding action. Recent graduate Annabelle Espinoza, who was directly in front of the shooting, said staff at that game did all they could and supported extra screening including metal detectors and ID checks, while community advocate Nadine Escalante of Concerned Parents of Education said she saw too little visible security in the stands at another district game last Friday.

**Bakersfield police screened more than 700 vehicles and arrested one person during Friday’s DUI checkpoint operation,** according to KGET 17. The high-volume screening was part of the department’s ongoing traffic safety push, and even a single arrest can matter when it stops an impaired driver before they cause harm. No other details about the operation were released.

**A 22-year-old man was killed on his birthday last Saturday when a car being pursued by Bakersfield police struck him in Oildale,** 23ABC reports. Kevin Daniel Stevens was hit near the corner of Airport Drive and Olive Drive after the fleeing vehicle swerved to avoid spike strips. His aunt, Chanel Stevens, said he had called the family the day before, telling them he was working to overcome drug addiction and make his way home; his mother had died just two months earlier, and his aunt questioned how the pursuit was handled. Police have not yet responded to a request for comment.

**City officials say gun-related homicides in Bakersfield are down so far this year despite the deadly Independence High shooting,** according to Bakersfield Now. The statistic stands in contrast to the public anxiety that followed the Aug. 21 game, though officials acknowledged the numbers do nothing to ease the grief of families affected by violence. The report did not include specific figures.

**Dignity Health is offering free flu vaccines at locations throughout Kern County during September,** KGET 17 says. The health system is making the shots available with no out-of-pocket cost to help families prepare for the fall flu season. Exact clinic locations and times were not listed in the report, so residents are encouraged to contact Dignity Health for the nearest site.

**A nearly $7 million grant will fund a package of aerospace and defense projects across Eastern Kern County,** 23ABC reports. The Space, Defense, & Satellites Project Cluster brings together Cal State Bakersfield, the Mojave Air and Space Port, and the Griffiss Institute, and includes upgrades to the space port, a new innovation hub on the CSUB campus, and improvements to an engineering workshop in Ridgecrest that will be open to local entrepreneurs and startups. Justin Salters of the Griffiss Institute said the three connected projects are designed to grow the region’s aerospace sector and create hundreds of construction and long-term jobs, with construction expected to begin soon.

## Something good

Dignity Health is stepping up for flu season with free vaccines at locations throughout Kern County this September, a practical boost for families who want to stay healthy. And while the news cycle has been heavy, the nearly $7 million aerospace and defense investment heading to Eastern Kern is a bright economic sign — it means upgrades to the Mojave Air and Space Port, a new innovation hub at CSUB, and a Ridgecrest workshop for local startups, with hundreds of jobs expected. For anyone carrying a heavy weight, KGET 17 also reminds residents that the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline is available with Kern County-specific ways to seek help. Good things are brewing, and help is out there.

## Coming up this week

Looking at the week ahead, there are a couple of public meetings worth putting on the calendar. The Fire Civil Service Commission meets Monday, Sept. 14, at 3 p.m. On Wednesday, Sept. 16, the Bakersfield City Council has two sessions: meeting 330 gets underway at 3:30 p.m., followed by meeting 515 at 5:15 p.m. Both are open to the public.

For entertainment, the Fox Theater is hosting a busy stretch. Comedian Justin Willman brings his “One for the Ages” tour Thursday night, Sept. 10. Max Amini performs live on Saturday, Sept. 12, and country singer Clay Walker rolls into town Sunday, Sept. 13, for the “Doin’ What I Love” tour. Next Monday, Sept. 14, the Cults & Classics series screens the Coen brothers’ “Fargo,” and the week closes out with “It’s A 2000s Party” on Friday, Sept. 18. Check the theater’s website for ticket availability and showtimes.
